decisions.decision: Separate GET /api/file/raw endpoint for edit mode instead of re-using the HTML preview endpoint
inputs: preview returns escaped HTML in a <pre>; edit mode needs the original bytes

alternatives_considered.option: parse the escaped HTML back to text in JS
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: fragile — anything in the rendered chrome (file-path div, actions row) would need stripping

alternatives_considered.option: return raw text + HTML bundled in one response
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: conflates two concerns; breaks the clean HTML-fragment-returning pattern used elsewhere

decisions.weighting_logic: One endpoint, one content type, clean separation. The extra round-trip on edit-click is cheap (localhost).

decisions.decision: Disabled-skills state in a plain-text .disabled file (one name per line), not JSON
inputs: user should be able to inspect/edit this from a plain text editor
the list is flat — no structured metadata needed

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: premature structure; if we later need metadata (last-enabled timestamp, etc.) we can upgrade

decisions.weighting_logic: Plain text is the project's language. Save JSON for when the fields demand it.

decisions.decision: Dedicated sidebar 'skills' section rather than inline toggles in the file tree
inputs: file tree re-renders every 10s via htmx poll — any local UI state would be clobbered
skills are a first-class product concept deserving UI space

alternatives_considered.option: toggle icons beside each SKILL.md in the tree
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: pollutes a generic browser with skill-specific semantics

alternatives_considered.option: toggle in the preview pane when viewing a SKILL.md
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: discovery sucks — user has to click into each skill to toggle it

decisions.weighting_logic: Skills as a separate vertical section in the sidebar gives them a stable home and scales to other first-class concepts (requests, next).

decisions.decision: Auto-load .rness/policies/*.md into system prompt under a # Policies section
inputs: v0.01 spec said skills auto-load but policies were 'user-populated, not auto-loaded'
but the Requests tracking system needs the convention in the prompt for the agent to comply

alternatives_considered.option: embed the requests convention in paradigms/default.md
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: conflates paradigm (how sessions work) with policy (what must happen); paradigm file would balloon over time

alternatives_considered.option: require user to manually reference policies from their paradigm
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: defeats the purpose of shipping a sensible default

decisions.weighting_logic: Policies are small, orthogonal to paradigms, and parallel to skills. Auto-load is the natural pattern.
decisions.downstream_impact: v0.02 users with existing projects can drop a .md file into .rness/policies/ and it's live on the next message.

decisions.decision: Date format YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM (sortable) rather than user's proposed MM_DD_YYYY-HH-MM
inputs: filename listings sort alphabetically; MM_DD_YYYY cross-year ordering breaks

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: asked them; they approved the switch

decisions.weighting_logic: Sortable filenames are a force multiplier for a paradigm that lives in the filesystem.

decisions.decision: Mark-done is a UI action only — agent cannot move files into requests/done/ itself
inputs: spec: the move IS the user's confirmation

alternatives_considered.option: agent uses shell mv when user confirms in chat
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: adds a failure mode where agent prematurely moves without real confirmation; also weakens the sense that 'done' is a ceremonial act

decisions.weighting_logic: The move is the approval. Keep it in the human's hands.

decisions.decision: Mark-done button is rendered by the server inside the preview fragment (when path matches .rness/requests/*.md) — not by frontend inspection
inputs: server owns path-classification (_is_request_file); frontend should not duplicate that logic

alternatives_considered.option: JS checks path prefix and adds button
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: logic duplication — if we ever rename or nest the folder, we'd have to fix two places

decisions.weighting_logic: Single source of truth for what counts as a 'request'.

decisions.decision: No conflict detection / locking on inline editor (last-write-wins)
inputs: v0.02 scope is 'get the feature shipped'; races are rare on localhost-single-user

alternatives_considered.option: send mtime on GET, reject POST if mtime changed
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: adds a field to the edit flow without observed value; the agent typically writes via write_file (not the editor) so the race window is narrow

decisions.weighting_logic: Ship and watch. If the user hits a lost-edit issue in practice, add mtime check then.
